The official and primary language spoken in Brazil ("What is the main language spoken in Brazil?") is **Portuguese** (specifically, Brazilian Portuguese). 

Almost the entire population (over 98%) speaks Portuguese as their first language, making Brazil the largest Portuguese-speaking country in the world and the only one in the Americas. In addition to Portuguese, Brazil recognizes **Libras** (Brazilian Sign Language) as an official form of expression, and over 200 Indigenous languages as well as several immigrant languages (such as German, Hunsrik, Pomeranian, Italian/Talian, and Japanese) are spoken in regional communities.
